llm.summary: The skill mostly matches its Pixmind image-generation purpose, but it sends Pixmind credentials and user prompts to a different disclosed domain and logs sensitive prompt/result data.

dimensions.detail: Fallback scripts read PIXMIND_API_KEY and send it with prompts and optional reference-image URLs to https://aihub-admin.aimix.pro, while the credential guidance points users to pixmind.io; that processor relationship is not explained in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install-time hooks, dependency installation, remote code loading, or package-manager execution were found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill names the Pixmind tools and limits fallback scripts to hosts without native tools, but it does not declare allowed tools in frontmatter and includes a broad trigger for Pixmind image requests.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, privilege escalation, or broad local access was found, but fallback scripts print prompts, generated URLs, and full API responses to stdout.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifact is coherent with generating and editing images through Pixmind, including model routing, paid-call approval guidance, generation, and task-status polling.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with Pixmind prompts, reference-image URLs, and the PIXMIND_API_KEY being used with the documented aihub-admin.aimix.pro endpoint. Prefer the native Pixmind Builder tools over the fallback scripts, avoid sensitive prompts or signed private image URLs, and be aware that fallback script output may be retained in terminal or agent logs.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Task-status polling is a normal part of asynchronous image generation; printing videoUrl and coverUrl fields is extra output handling, not evidence that the skill generates unrelated media.
[LP3] expected: The skill does not use an allowed-tools frontmatter field, but its instructions explicitly name the Pixmind generation/status tools and constrain fallback script use.
[SQP-1] expected: The trigger is tied to creating or modifying images through Pixmind and the workflow requires approval before a paid call, so it is not by itself a security concern.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese trigger examples and English fallback help text are locale limitations or documentation polish issues, not material security risks.
[T09] expected: Sending a provider API key and generation content to a remote image-generation API is purpose-aligned, but the artifact does not explain why a pixmind.io credential is submitted to aihub-admin.aimix.pro.
[T09] unexpected: Normal fallback execution logs the full prompt and complete API responses, which is unnecessary for image generation and can expose sensitive prompts or signed asset URLs in logs.
[T09] expected: Polling and generation parameter handling are expected, but the fallback scripts lack local count validation and bounded polling limits, creating possible credit or quota surprises.
